units.text: Fluorescent light, a dozen washers turning slow, lukewarm steam on the windows.
Four people wait out their cycles.
This is the last time they will all be in the same room, though none of them knows it yet.
units.name: NARRATOR

units.text: My mother said never wash a dead man's shirts. I said, Ma, they're only shirts.
units.name: LORETTA

units.text: Cheap soap makes more suds. Doesn't make it clean.
units.name: DEV
paren: not looking up from his phone, thumbing a message

units.text: Who's the guy outside? He's been standing by the bins for twenty minutes.
units.name: PRIYA
paren: holding a hot towel to her cheek, watching the door

units.text: Waiting on a dryer, probably. Everybody waits on something.
units.name: OSWALD
paren: stirring a paper cup of coffee, shrugging

units.text: The bell over the door jingles.
A TALL MAN IN A DRIPPING YELLOW SLICKER steps in, carrying a laundry bag that is much too heavy and much too still.
Calm lasts exactly as long as the first drip hitting the tile.
units.name: NARRATOR

units.text: Evening. Any machines free? I've a bit of a mess to wash.
units.name: THE TALL MAN
paren: setting the bag down gently, smiling

units.text: Every washer in the room stops spinning at once.
